rows.grounds: refers to the divya grade of practitioner
sandhi form of doṣaḥ before atra
compound: śiva+ājñā; acting under divine injunction

items.question: Why is there no fault in the divine or supreme heroic grades when acting by Śiva's command?
premises: The context concerns the divine grade of practitioner.
The context also concerns the supreme heroic grade.
Action performed by Śiva's command removes fault.
items.inference: Therefore, in the divine or supreme heroic grades there is no fault here because of Śiva's command.
items.plain_english: In the divine or in the supreme heroic grade, there is no fault here, because it is by Śiva's command.

items.question: What prompts the request for the supreme lord to explain the nature of the practitioner grades?
premises: The speaker addresses the supreme lord directly.
The speaker asks the lord to tell.
The speaker's mind is eager to hear.
items.inference: Therefore, the eager speaker requests the supreme lord to explain the matter.
items.plain_english: Tell me, O supreme Lord; my mind is eager to hear.

items.question: What defining qualities characterize the divine grade practitioner in conduct and presence?
premises: The divine practitioner captivates all minds.
The divine practitioner speaks in measured words.
The divine practitioner remains steady in posture.
items.inference: Therefore, the divine practitioner is marked by captivating presence, measured speech, and steadiness.
items.plain_english: The divine one captivates all minds, speaks with measure, and remains steady in posture.

items.question: How does the divine practitioner relate to the guru and to fear in all situations?
premises: The divine practitioner is reverent at the guru's lotus feet.
The divine practitioner is free from fear.
This fearlessness applies everywhere.
items.inference: Therefore, the divine practitioner combines reverence for the guru with universal fearlessness.
items.plain_english: Reverent at the lotus feet of the guru, he is everywhere devoid of fear.

rows.grounds: sandhi form of saḥ+aham; emphatic identification

items.question: Why is further elaboration unnecessary when describing the fully qualified divine practitioner?
premises: The divine practitioner is endowed with all qualities.
Such a practitioner is identified emphatically.
Many words add nothing essential.
items.inference: Therefore, the divine practitioner, endowed with all qualities, needs no further description.
items.plain_english: The divine one is endowed with all qualities—what more need be said with many words?

rows.grounds: compound: pañca+tattva; the five ritual elements

items.question: What qualities and ritual disposition distinguish the heroic practitioner described here?
premises: The practitioner is talkative, strong, and pure.
The practitioner delights in the five elements.
This delight is constant.
items.inference: Therefore, the heroic practitioner is characterized by strength, purity, and constant delight in the five elements.
uncertainties: vācālaḥ may mean talkative or eloquent; rendered as talkative
items.plain_english: He is talkative, strong, and pure, always delighting in the five elements.

items.question: What ethical commitment defines the heroic practitioner's relation to virtuous people?
premises: The practitioner is great-minded.
The practitioner is always devoted to protecting good people.
This is stated as a defining trait.
items.inference: Therefore, the heroic practitioner is noble and constantly devoted to the protection of the virtuous.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, he is great-minded and always devoted to the protection of good people.

items.question: What exalted identity is attributed to the heroic practitioner endowed with many virtues?
premises: The heroic practitioner is endowed with many qualities.
These qualities have been described above.
Such a hero is identified as Rudra himself.
items.inference: Therefore, the fully qualified heroic practitioner is Rudra himself.
items.plain_english: O beloved, the hero endowed with many such qualities is Rudra himself.

rows.grounds: compound: pāpa+citta; those with impure minds
compound: pañca+tattva+vinindaka; those who revile the five elements

items.question: Which kinds of people are identified as lowly and opposed to the five elements?
premises: Some people are described as lowly.
Some people are described as sin-minded.
Some people revile the five elements.
items.inference: Therefore, the lowly include the sin-minded and those who revile the five elements.
items.plain_english: The lowly, the sin-minded, and those who revile the five elements—

rows.grounds: compound: khara+upamā; compared to a donkey
sandhi form of kecit; another subset
compound: śūkara+upamā; compared to a pig

items.question: How are the fallen lowly practitioners metaphorically characterized in this teaching?
premises: Some fallen ones are likened to donkeys.
Some fallen ones are likened to pigs.
These comparisons mark their degraded state.
items.inference: Therefore, the fallen lowly are metaphorically described as donkey-like and pig-like.
items.plain_english: Some of these fallen ones are like donkeys, and some are like pigs.

rows.grounds: refers to the lowly described above
compound: devī+arcana; ritual worship of the goddess

items.question: Can goddess-worship or spiritual attainment arise for those who revile the five elements?
premises: The subjects are the lowly revilers described above.
Goddess-worship and attainment are considered.
The question implies impossibility.
items.inference: Therefore, for such people there can be no goddess-worship, attainment, or valid counting.
uncertainties: gaṇanaṃ may refer to counting of mantras or enumeration; rendered as counting
items.plain_english: How could there be goddess-worship, attainment, or even counting for such as these?

rows.grounds: compound: parama+artha+bahiṣ+kṛta; cast outside the supreme goal

items.question: What is the ultimate spiritual status of those excluded from proper practice?
premises: Such people are excluded in every way.
They are cast outside the supreme truth.
This exclusion is total.
items.inference: Therefore, they are completely excluded from the supreme truth.
items.plain_english: O fair one, they are in every way excluded, cast out from the supreme truth.

rows.grounds: compound: paśu+bhāva; the paśu condition, sandhi before ca
inherently or by its own nature

items.question: How is the animal nature inherently characterized in this doctrinal declaration?
premises: The animal nature is declared in the teaching.
It is described as lowly.
This lowliness is inherent and constant.
items.inference: Therefore, the animal nature is inherently and always declared to be lowly.
items.plain_english: Indeed, the animal nature is declared to be lowly, as it is always so by itself.

items.question: Why are offerings made from the animal nature not accepted by the deity?
premises: The deity does not recognize the animal-natured offerer.
Recognition is required for acceptance.
What is offered from that state is therefore not accepted.
items.inference: Therefore, because the deity does not recognize it, what is offered by the animal-natured one is not truly accepted.
items.plain_english: The deity does not truly recognize it; therefore, what is offered is not accepted.

rows.grounds: sandhi form of sūryaḥ; agent of illumination
sandhi form of andhakāram; object dispelled

items.question: What analogy illustrates the power that dispels the darkness of the animal nature?
premises: The sun dispels darkness.
This dispelling happens in a moment.
The analogy implies a powerful removing force.
items.inference: Therefore, just as the sun instantly destroys darkness, so a higher force can dispel the animal nature.
items.plain_english: Just as the sun destroys darkness in a single moment—

rows.grounds: sandhi form of yaḥ; relative subject

items.question: Who serves as the protector of the declared animal nature in the Kali age?
premises: The animal nature has been declared.
The context is the Kali age.
A protector for that state is questioned.
items.inference: Therefore, the teaching raises the question of who protects the animal nature in the Kali age.
items.plain_english: Who, indeed, is the protector of that declared animal nature in the Kali age?

items.question: What attitude toward Śiva's teaching should guide one regarding the animal nature?
premises: Śiva has declared a teaching.
That teaching is to be regarded as truth.
One should hold this conviction firmly.
items.inference: Therefore, one should consider as truth whatever has been declared by Śiva.
items.plain_english: Considering as truth whatever has been declared by Śiva—

items.question: What is promised when the conduct of the animal-natured practitioner is explained?
premises: The speaker will tell the conduct of that practitioner.
The listener is urged to hear quickly.
The explanation destroys doubt.
items.inference: Therefore, the prescribed conduct will be explained in a way that removes doubt.
items.plain_english: I will now tell you his conduct; listen quickly, for it destroys doubt.

rows.grounds: compound: ṛtu+snātā; a woman purified after her period

items.question: Under what restriction must the animal-natured practitioner approach a woman with desire?
premises: Contact with a woman is considered.
The contact is motivated by desire.
The woman must be ritually bathed after menses.
items.inference: Therefore, the paśu practitioner should touch a woman with desire only if she has completed the post-menses bath.
items.plain_english: He should touch a woman with desire only if she has bathed after her menstrual period.

rows.grounds: compound: matsya+māṃsa; prohibited foods in this context
sandhi form of pāśavaḥ; paśu practitioners

items.question: What dietary restriction is prescribed for practitioners of the animal nature?
premises: The rule applies to animal-natured practitioners.
Fish and meat are specified.
The abandonment must be constant.
items.inference: Therefore, animal-natured practitioners should always abandon fish and meat.
items.plain_english: Those of animal nature should always abandon fish and meat.

rows.grounds: compound: āhāra+artha; purpose of going home

items.question: Where should the animal-natured practitioner dwell and for what purpose may he leave?
premises: The practitioner should always stay in the temple.
Going to the house is permitted for food.
Residence and departure are regulated.
items.inference: Therefore, the paśu practitioner should dwell in the temple and go home only for food.
items.plain_english: He should always stay in the temple and go home only for the sake of food.

rows.grounds: verb of seeking; negated by following na

items.question: How should the animal-natured practitioner relate to sovereignty whether absent or present?
premises: One should not seek sovereignty.
Sovereignty may already exist.
If it exists, it should not be abandoned.
items.inference: Therefore, the paśu practitioner should neither seek sovereignty nor abandon it if already present.
items.plain_english: He should not seek sovereignty; but if it exists, he should not abandon it.

rows.grounds: compound: kārpa+droha; hostility toward the weak or wretched
compound: ahaṅkāra+ādika; egoism and similar faults

items.question: What inner and social faults must the animal-natured practitioner cast away?
premises: Enmity toward the weak must be cast away.
Egoism and similar faults must be cast away.
All such faults are included.
items.inference: Therefore, the practitioner should cast away all hostility to the weak, egoism, and related faults.
uncertainties: kārpa+drohān interpreted as enmity toward the weak; alternative readings possible
items.plain_english: Then he should cast away all enmity toward the weak, egoism, and the like.

rows.grounds: verb of giving initiation; negated by following na

items.question: Why is the animal-natured practitioner prohibited from conferring initiation on others?
premises: The subject is the animal-natured practitioner.
Conferring initiation is considered.
The prohibition is absolute.
items.inference: Therefore, the animal-natured practitioner should never confer initiation.
items.plain_english: O supreme Goddess, one of animal nature should never confer initiation.
